jobs.prompt: On 2026-10-24 a scratch checkout holding the only copy of a project ledger (.swarm/project/tickets.json, .swarm/runs, approvals) disappeared right after its pull request was merged with swarm merge (gh pr merge --delete-branch). Cause unproven. Make it impossible for cleanup code to delete a checkout that holds swarm state. 1) New tools/state-guard.mjs exporting holdsSwarmState(dir, {fs, registryFile}) (true when dir/.swarm/project/tickets.json exists, or dir/.swarm/runs has any run, or dir is a root listed in the user projects registry ~/.project-swarm/projects.json (injectable path), or dir contains a .project-swarm.json with a ledger), assertNotStateHolder(dir, caller) that throws an error with code state-holder-refused and a one-line warning naming the dir and caller, and recordDeletion({dir, caller, outcome, home, now}) that appends one JSON line to ~/.project-swarm/deletions.log (mode 0600; never throws; PROJECT_SWARM_HOME override for tests). 2) Use it before every recursive removal or git worktree remove of a whole checkout in tools/gc.mjs (the scratch category and removeGitWorktree), tools/swarm/core-71.mjs (scratch cleanup), and the forget --scratch path in tools/swarm.mjs ONLY if it can be done by calling the guard from an existing helper without editing tools/swarm.mjs (skip it otherwise and say so in a code comment in state-guard.mjs). Refuse and warn (a skipped result with reason state-holder) instead of deleting; log every deletion attempt, allowed or refused, with recordDeletion. gc must also never consider a state holder as a scratch candidate. 3) tools/merge-guard.mjs: do not pass --delete-branch to gh pr merge when the head branch is checked out in any worktree (git worktree list --porcelain, injectable exec) whose directory holds swarm state; instead merge without --delete-branch and delete only the remote branch with gh api -X DELETE repos/OWNER/NAME/git/refs/heads/BRANCH (encode the branch path), and report localBranch: kept in the result. Otherwise behave exactly as today. 4) tests/state-guard.test.mjs with injected fakes and temp dirs only: holdsSwarmState for each marker, refusal in gc scratch candidate selection and apply, refusal in the core-71 path where testable, deletion log lines, merge-guard args with and without a state-holding worktree. Keep every existing test passing.

Protect the ticket ledger against losing its checkout. Backups that live inside the checkout (tools/state-backup.mjs) die with it, so add backups OUTSIDE any checkout. 1) tools/ledger-backup.mjs: backupLedger(root, {reason, home, now, fs}) copies .swarm/project/tickets.json, tickets.log, the scope snapshot markdown files in that folder, brain-ledger.ndjson and backlog.json (whichever exist; never security-key or any secret file) into ~/.project-swarm/ledger-backups/<key>/ where key = <basename of root>-<first 12 hex of sha256 of the real path>; each snapshot is a folder named <UTC timestamp>-<first 8 hex of the ledger sha256> with a meta.json (root path, reason, ledger sha256, ticket count, done count, approved hash, version); skip when the ledger content hash equals the newest snapshot; keep the newest 50 change snapshots, plus one daily snapshot per UTC day kept for 90 days in a daily/ subfolder (copy the day's last change). Folders mode 0700, files 0600, atomic writes (temp then rename), never follows symlinks, never throws into the caller (returns {ok:false, reason}); PROJECT_SWARM_HOME overrides home for tests. 2) Hook: tools/tickets.mjs writeLedger calls backupLedger after a successful write (fire and wait, best effort, 5 second cap, ignored errors) so every ledger change is backed up; skip when an env PROJECT_SWARM_NO_LEDGER_BACKUP is set (tests that write many ledgers must stay fast: also skip when the root is under the OS temp dir unless PROJECT_SWARM_HOME is set explicitly). 3) tools/ledger-cli.mjs exports runLedgerCommand(root, args) and tools/safety-commands.mjs (which already handles the backup command) delegates to it for `swarm backup ledger ...` (do NOT edit tools/swarm.mjs): `swarm backup ledger now`, `swarm backup ledger list [--all]` (snapshots for this root's key; --all lists every key with its recorded root path, so a ledger can be found after the checkout is gone), `swarm backup ledger restore [ID|latest] [--from KEY] [--into DIR] [--yes]`: restores the snapshot into DIR (default the current --root), refuses to overwrite a non-empty existing ledger without --yes, takes a backup of the current ledger first, verifies the sha256 after the copy, and prints done/total per stage afterwards. A later change will add the short alias swarm ledger. 4) tests/ledger-backup.test.mjs with temp dirs and injected home: snapshot on change, dedupe on identical content, retention of 50 and the daily copy, never copies secrets, restore round trip through runSafetyCommand with the hash check, refuse without --yes, list --all after the source root is deleted, the writeLedger hook is best effort when the home is unwritable. 5) docs/ledger-backups.md: where backups live, retention, restore steps. Keep every existing test passing.
